question.value: Trace the cold molecular gas component and infer H2 masses, star-formation efficiencies, and gas fractions in seven high-redshift radio galaxies (z = 2.9 - 4.5) using ALMA [C I](1-0) and MUSE observations.

evidence.quote: We present Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) neutral carbon, [C i](1-0), line observations that probe molecular hydrogen gas (H 2 ) within seven radio galaxies at 𝑧 = 2 . 9 − 4 . 5

With the goal of simultaneously tracing the ionised and molecular gas components of the extended halos of HzRGs, we have defined a sub-sample of seven HzRGs that are observable both in Ly 𝛼 with MUSE and in [C i] with ALMA.
The radio galaxies in our sample were observed in ALMA bands 3 (Kerr et al. 2014) and 4 (Asayama et al. 2014) during ALMA Cycle 3 under the project ID 2015.1.00530.S (PI: De Breuck)
This paper also makes use of the following ALMA observations: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00530.S.

findings_qualitative.value: Faint [C I](1-0) emission (2-3 sigma) is detected in 4 out of 7 high-z radio galaxies, while 3 out of 7 are undetected.

evidence.quote: We detect faint [C i] emission in four out of seven sources.

evidence.loc: 5.1 Neutral carbon within the host galaxies
evidence.quote: At least three HzRGs in our observations are not detected in [C i], while the remaining four have 2 − 3 𝜎 level line detections.

findings_qualitative.value: Two detected sources (MRC 0943-242 and 4C+03.24) exhibit very narrow [C I] line widths (40-50 km s^-1) that likely trace individual molecular gas clouds rather than full host galaxy rotation, whereas TN J0121+1320 and 4C+19.71 show broader widths (179-565 km s^-1).

evidence.quote: In two of these galaxies, we discover narrow line emission of full width at half maximum ≲ 100 km s −1 which may trace emission from bright kpc-scale gas clouds within the ISM.

evidence.loc: 5.1 Neutral carbon within the host galaxies
evidence.quote: In MRC 0943-242 and 4C+03.24, the dispersions range from 40-50 km s −1 and are insufficiently broad to cover the rotational velocity of the host galaxy and can therefore only trace single molecular clouds within the galaxy.

findings_qualitative.value: HzRGs in this sample have lower molecular gas masses and lower gas fractions (f_gas < 0.2) and higher star-formation efficiencies than typical high-z star-forming and submillimeter galaxies, caused either by gas depletion from earlier starbursts or removal via jet-driven AGN feedback.

evidence.quote: Our results imply that the observed faintness in carbon emission is representative of a decline in molecular gas supply from previous star-formation epochs and/or a displacement of molecular gas from the ISM due to jet-powered outflows.
Generally, we find that high- 𝑧 radio galaxies have 𝑓 gas < 0 . 2 and relatively high SFE’s of 4 − 45 Gyr −1 .

claims.hypothesis: [C I](1-0) line emission can trace cold molecular gas (H2) in the host galaxies of z = 2.9 - 4.5 radio galaxies.
claims.experiment: Observed seven HzRGs in ALMA Bands 3 and 4 targeting [C I](1-0), extracted 1D spectra at the host galaxy positions known from VLA and Spitzer, and fit Gaussian line profiles.
claims.result: Faint (2-3 sigma) [C I](1-0) detections in 4/7 galaxies with M_H2,[CI] = (0.49 - 2.60) x 10^10 M_sun, and 5-sigma upper limits of M_H2,[CI] < (0.53 - 1.08) x 10^10 M_sun in 3/7 galaxies.
claims.finding: Molecular gas in these HzRGs is fainter and less massive than previously reported for similar galaxies.

evidence.quote: We detect faint [C i] emission in four out of seven sources.
The molecular gas masses in our sample are relatively low in comparison to previously reported measures for similar galaxies which are 𝑀 H 2 , [C i] ≃(3 − 4) × 10 10 M ⊙ .

claims.hypothesis: Narrow [C I](1-0) line widths in some HzRGs trace localized molecular clouds, while broader lines trace global galaxy rotation/kinematics.
claims.experiment: Measured [C I](1-0) FWHM from Gaussian fits to 1D host-galaxy spectra and compared with galaxy rotational velocities and CO detections.
claims.result: MRC 0943-242 and 4C+03.24 show narrow FWHM of 40 +- 14 and 47 +- 16 km s^-1, whereas 4C+19.71 and TN J0121+1320 have FWHM of 179 +- 60 and 565 +- 194 km s^-1.
claims.finding: Narrow 40-50 km s^-1 dispersions cannot cover the full rotational velocity of the host galaxy and only trace single/bright kpc-scale molecular clouds, while broader lines trace global disk kinematics.

evidence.quote: In two of these galaxies, we discover narrow line emission of full width at half maximum ≲ 100 km s −1 which may trace emission from bright kpc-scale gas clouds within the ISM.

evidence.loc: 5.1 Neutral carbon within the host galaxies
evidence.quote: In MRC 0943-242 and 4C+03.24, the dispersions range from 40-50 km s −1 and are insufficiently broad to cover the rotational velocity of the host galaxy and can therefore only trace single molecular clouds within the galaxy.

claims.hypothesis: Low molecular gas fractions in z ~ 3.5 radio galaxies are caused by AGN jet-driven mechanical feedback and/or gas depletion from an earlier rapid starburst epoch.
claims.experiment: Calculated gas fractions (f_gas) and star-formation efficiencies (SFE) for the HzRG sample and compared them on the SFE-f_gas and SFR-M* planes with literature SFGs and SMGs.
claims.result: HzRGs exhibit low gas fractions (f_gas < 0.2, with three below 10%) and high SFEs (3.3 - 42.6 Gyr^-1), sitting mostly near or slightly below the star-forming Main Sequence.
claims.finding: Both prior starburst gas depletion and negative kinetic AGN feedback remain viable explanations for the low molecular gas content, but current data cannot conclusively distinguish between them.

evidence.loc: 5.4.2 AGN feedback effects on cold gas
evidence.quote: In summary, due to the observed faintness of the molecular gas as traced via [C i] in the AGN host galaxies galaxies with high stellar masses and powerful radio jets, we tentatively conclude that AGN feedback may be the cause for the low molecular gas fractions. However, we can not rule out an earlier starburst as the cause of the depletion.
Our current data is too shallow to allow for a proper conclusion on which mechanism is primarily responsible for the low molecular gas fractions we have observed in our sample of radio galaxies.

why_this_data.value: ALMA Bands 3 and 4 trace [C I](1-0) at z = 2.9 - 4.5, which is resilient to cosmic-ray photodissociation in jetted AGN and matches the redshift window where VLT/MUSE detects rest-UV lines (Ly-alpha, He II).

evidence.quote: Selecting [C i] as a tracer may be especially wise given that radio galaxies have jetted AGN that produce high-energy cosmic rays which are capable of photodissociating CO in molecular gas.

the Atacama Large Millimeter-submillimeter Array (ALMA) has frequency bands 3 and 4 which are best suited for probing emission from this atomic transition at a redshift range of 𝑧 = 2 . 9 − 4 . 5 where rest-UV lines are detectable within the observational window of the Multi-Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE).

why_this_method.value: Natural uv-weighting (robust = 2) without uv-tapering was chosen to maximise S/N, and fixed apertures at known radio core / Spitzer host positions were used to include the central host galaxy and ensure stable Gaussian fit convergence.

evidence.quote: For the imaging, we used the data reduction pipeline (casa-6.2.1.7 and a natural uv -weighting ( robust parameter 2) to optimise the signal-to-noise ratio (S/N) at the expense of spatial resolution.

We select this aperture size to ensure that (i) the full central part of the host galaxy is included, and (ii) the extracted 1D spectra have sufficient S/N to provide a stable convergence of the fitting algorithm.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gaussian uv-tapering of the 12m ALMA data (with 2, 3, and 4 arcsec widths) was attempted to recover extended CGM emission, but rejected because increased noise reduced the overall S/N for all sources except MRC 0943-242.

evidence.quote: we also made an attempt at tapering the 12m uv -data with 2 ′′, 3 ′′, and 4 ′′ Gaussian width options. For all sources, with the exception of MRC 0943-292, an increase in noise due to the reduced amount of data decreased the S/N data overall. Hence, we opted to continue forward with the untapered images

limitations_admitted.value: Low S/N (2-3 sigma) of the [C I](1-0) detections leads to large redshift and line width uncertainties and prevents detailed kinematic modelling or distinguishing between starburst depletion and AGN feedback.

evidence.quote: Our current data is too shallow to allow for a proper conclusion on which mechanism is primarily responsible for the low molecular gas fractions we have observed in our sample of radio galaxies.

limitations_admitted.value: Neglecting the neutral H I gas component when computing M_gas may underestimate total gas mass by up to a factor of two.

evidence.quote: Due to the lack of systematic measurements, we neglect the H i component, which may lead to an under-estimate of 𝑀 gas by a factor up to two.

limitations_admitted.value: Assumed conversion factors (alpha_CO, X_[CI], Q_10) have large uncertainties for individual galaxies.

evidence.loc: 5.2 Comparing CO and [C i]-derived molecular gas in high- 𝑧 radio galaxies
evidence.quote: As expected, the [C i] and CO gas estimates do not lead to equivalent results due to the assumptions on 𝛼 CO and X [C i] and Q 10 , which are more appropriate for populations of galaxies, but have large uncertainties for individual galaxies.

limitations_admitted.value: Stellar masses from Spitzer photometry are often conservative upper limits due to possible hot dust torus contamination at rest-frame 1.6 um.

evidence.quote: We note that the stellar masses reported by Seymour et al. (2007) and De Breuck et al. (2010) are often upper limits due to potential contributions from the hot dust torus emission to the rest-frame 1.6 𝜇 m photometry.

referee_caveats_inferred: All four [C I](1-0) detections are marginal (2-3 sigma), meaning line fluxes, FWHMs, and derived H2 masses are highly sensitive to channel binning and baseline/continuum subtraction choices.

There is an internal inconsistency in the text regarding the [C I] spectral extraction aperture: Sections 3.1 and 4.3 specify a 2 arcsec diameter aperture, whereas the Figure 3 caption and Section 5.2 state a 1 arcsec aperture.
Simultaneously observed 13CO(4-3) spectral windows are mentioned in Sections 2 and 3.1, but no results or upper limits are reported for 13CO(4-3).

In the abstract and Conclusions, the upper limit on M_H2 for non-detections is summarized as < 0.65 x 10^10 M_sun, whereas Table 3 and Section 4.4 list upper limits up to < 1.08 x 10^10 M_sun (0.65 x 10^10 M_sun is actually the detection value for 4C+03.24).
